text:
anya: quick Q — where is the canonical place to grab p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec when doing a TTFT latency deep-dive? I need links to dashboards + a sample promql

devon: for dashboards: https://grafana.redwood-infra.com/d/latency-overview/latency-summary (panel names: 'TTFT by model', 'Tokens/sec by route')

sam: +1 to that. also check 'request-slice' dropdown (top-right) to slice by model/version/route. saves a ton of time.

leo: if you're running a trace, Jaeger samples are in the 'TTFT traces' dashboard (bookmark panel -> 'Open in Jaeger').

anya: perfect — any recommended PromQL snippets for p95 and tokens/sec I can paste into a doc?

devon: sure, quick ones: fenced for copy

devon: ```promql
# p95 TTFT (request duration ms)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference"}[5m])) by (le, model)) * 1000

# tokens/sec (per route)
sum(rate(tokens_generated_total{job="inference"}[1m])) by (route)
```

sam: note: use 5m for p95 to smooth noise; for alerting maybe 1m for spike detection. also multiply by 1000 to get ms.

leo: watch out for batching and cache hits — they skew tokens/sec and TTFT. add a tag filter to exclude cache: `| cache_hit="true"` when you want cold-only analysis.

anya: good call. how do we get cold-only p99?

devon: add `cache_hit="false"` (or `cache="miss"` depending on metric) and use histogram_quantile(0.99,...). e.g.

devon: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference",cache_hit="false"}[5m])) by (le, model, route)) * 1000
```

sam: for correlating token rates with TTFT, plot tokens/sec (1m) and p95 (5m) on the same time window but different y-axes — you'll often see a lag when throughput increases.

anya: any existing bookmarks/panels I can grab instead of building from scratch?

leo: yes — dashboard panels have 'Share -> Direct link to panel'. I saved a few in the onboarding doc: https://confluence.redwood/team/obs/ttft-cheatsheet (see 'Panels to reuse' section).

obs-bot: deployed alert: TTFT_p95_high for model=redwood-rlf at 2026-02-11T17:40:02Z — ping @eng-runtime on rotation.

anya: thanks, that alert popped during my repro earlier. Is there a recommended tuning baseline for p95 before we escalate?

devon: baseline depends on model/route. rough guide in the cheatsheet: p95 < 250ms for lightweight routing, < 800ms for long-context completions. put alerts at +2x baseline for initial avoidable noise, then tighten after a week.

sam: and for tokens/sec, alert only on sustained >3x baseline over 5m for autoscale to kick in — short bursts are expected.

anya: can someone paste a short checklist I can use for triage when p95 spikes?

leo: simple triage checklist: 1) check tokens/sec for the route, 2) check cache_hit ratio, 3) open a sample trace (Jaeger), 4) look at pod-level CPU/GPU utilization, 5) check recent rolling deploys.

devon: adding panel/bookmark tips: enable 'time range -> change to 1h then hover with shift to inspect deltas' and add annotations for deploys.

anya: amazing, this is exactly what I needed. I'll update the doc and link these snippets. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: happy to review the doc once you have a draft, @anya

anya: will do, aim to post a PR to the onboarding page by EOD tomorrow.

leo: FYI I'm going to pin the grafana links in #eng-runtime-resources after your PR lands.
